title: Countably generated flat Mittag-Leffler modules are projective
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $P$ an $R$-module. Assume $P$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], Mittag-Leffler [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module], and countably generated: there is a countable subset $E\subseteq P$ such that every element of $P$ is a finite $R$-linear combination of elements of $E$. Then $P$ is projective over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact], tensoring with the flat module $P$ preserves exactness, including injectivity at the left end. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] it also preserves surjectivity at the right end. Thus it preserves every short exact sequence, which is precisely the hypothesis of [lem-kun-lazard-flat-module]. That node gives a small nonempty directed poset $I$, finite free modules $F_i\cong R^{r_i}$, and compatible maps exhibiting $P$ as their colimit.

Every $F_i\cong R^{r_i}$ is finitely presented, with presentation $R^0\to R^{r_i}\to F_i\to0$. Apply [lem-trf-ml-countable-colimit] using the assumed countable generation and tensor-product Mittag-Leffler property of $P$. Obtain a nonempty countable directed subset $J\subseteq I$ for which the restricted cocone still exhibits $P$ as colimit.

Enumerate $J$ by a sequence $j_1,j_2,\ldots$, repeating entries when $J$ is finite. Recursively choose $k_1=j_1$ and $k_{n+1}\in J$ above both $k_n$ and $j_{n+1}$. Set $G_n=F_{k_n}$ and use the inherited transitions. These indices are cofinal. To verify the colimit directly, a compatible family $a_n:G_n\to T$ extends to $F_j\to T$ by $a_n f_{j,k_n}$ whenever $j\le k_n$. Two such choices agree by passing to a larger sequence index; the same computation proves compatibility with every arrow of $J$. Conversely, restriction recovers $a_n$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] therefore exhibits $P$ as $\operatorname{colim}_{n\ge1}G_n$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-mittag-leffler-hom-systems] to this sequence of finite free, hence finitely presented, modules and its colimit $P$. For every $R$-module $N$, it says exactly that the inverse sequence $\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N)$ has eventually constant transition images, that is, is Mittag-Leffler as defined in [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system].

source.place: Tag 059X, Hom-system Mittag-Leffler assertion; Tags 059M and 059E (4).

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary short exact sequence $0\to N_1\xrightarrow{a}N_2\xrightarrow{b}N_3\to0$. For every $n$ the induced sequence $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N_1)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N_2)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N_3)\to0$ is exact. Indeed, choose a basis identifying $G_n$ with $R^{s_n}$; Hom becomes the finite power $N^{s_n}$. Injectivity and equality of kernel with image hold coordinatewise, and a tuple in $N_3^{s_n}$ lifts by choosing a preimage in $N_2$ of each of its finitely many coordinates. Precomposition with $G_n\to G_{n+1}$ commutes with postcomposition by $a,b$, so these sequences form a short exact sequence of inverse systems.

source.place: Tag 059X, finite-free Hom exactness, coordinate proof.

proof.text: The kernel inverse system $\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N_1)$ is Mittag-Leffler by step 4. All three systems are indexed by positive integers and the maps commute with transitions by step 5. Hence part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-limit-exact], applied to the underlying abelian groups, gives the short exact sequence of their inverse limits. The limit maps are $R$-linear because all component maps are; exactness of underlying groups is exactness of the $R$-modules.

For every $N$, map $h:P\to N$ to $(h\iota_n)_n$, where $\iota_n:G_n\to P$ are the colimit maps. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives a unique inverse map from every compatible family. Addition and scalar multiplication agree after restriction to every $G_n$, so this is an $R$-linear isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,N)\cong\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N)$. For $v:N\to N^\prime$, the equality $(vh)\iota_n=v(h\iota_n)$ proves naturality. These isomorphisms therefore identify the exact sequence of step 6 with the sequence obtained by applying $\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,-)$ to the arbitrary short exact sequence in step 5. Consequently this Hom functor is exact, so $P$ is projective by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].
